name: Styles P
notes: Subtraction is the style. Two-note motifs (`motifPitchCount` [2,3] — the lowest in this batch), the lowest melody register on this axis, "velocity flat by design" authored as a `velocityTiers` spread of about 26 rather than the parent's 89, and a harmony that genuinely does not move. ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set and is a description, not an exemption: the research says "static i or i–VII", so what varies across seeds is how long the loop sits on a chord (`chordDurationBeats` 2–16), which of three harmonic rhythms it uses, and where in a 36-semitone voicing register it lands — not what the chord is. Adding families this artist does not play would have been the dishonest way to reach the chord-variety floor. ⚠ The sustained sub is `mirror_kick` at `followRootsProb` 0.95 over a kick that plays 1 and 3&: two low roots a bar, which reads as sustained at 92 BPM. The engine's held-note rhythm emits one note per chord and over a static i that is one note. ⚠ The research says "no fills". This batch's anti-convergence fingerprint requires a `fills` cadence on every entry, so the cadence is there but the roll it triggers is authored to be the thinnest in the batch — `gapProb` 0.63 (highest here), `rampJitter` 5 (lowest here), `descendProb` 0.06. The fill cadence is the batch fingerprint; the roll content is the record. ⚠ `medium`, and the inferred parameters are the drum specifics — the research says the era and roster are documented but the numbers are partly inherited. ⚠ **The bass pool was widened after `bass.rs` measured it at 0.944 distinct against a floor of 0.95.** It was authored with NO passing tones, followRootsProb 0.95, anticipationProb 0.05 over register [24,40] — a faithful description of a sample-loop bass, and one that leaves a seed nothing to vary but root and octave. Now ["P5"], root lock 0.9, anticipation 0.18, register [24,44]. The line is still overwhelmingly root-on-kick; what changed is how many different records it can be, not how busy any one of them is. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 970 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary.
